lessons.title: Linguistic diversity and dialects
lessons.anelcac: Notions of linguistic diversity, dialects, names of languages, geographical classification
objectives: Becoming aware of the linguistic diversity of Cameroon (about 280 languages according to the LACAGEO Mini-Atlas)
Distinguish language, dialect and variant according to academic definitions
Naming Ngiemboon and locating it in the geographical classification of the languages of Cameroon
Adopt an attitude of respect towards all languages

teacher.intro: Lesson: Linguistic diversity and dialects. Module: Module I — Cameroonian linguistic diversity.
steps: **Setting the context:** Display the map of the Linguistic Mini-Atlas of Cameroon. Ask students which languages are spoken in their family.
**Exploration:** Have students read the definitions in the Mini-Atlas (language, dialect, patois, national language). Locate Ngiemboon in its linguistic region.
**Conceptualisation:** Explain the language / dialect distinction with examples: the Bulu, Ewondo, Eton and Mangisa dialects all belong to the Beti-Fang language (Mini-Atlas).
**Application:** Complete a table: name of the language, family, main region, ISO code.
**Assessment:** Each student gives an oral presentation of Ngiemboon, indicating family and region.
teacher.freedom: The LACAGEO Mini-Atlas (2013) distinguishes about 280 living languages in Cameroon. The exact number varies according to the criteria (SIL: 274, Ethnologue: 279). Value all the languages cited.
teacher.tips: The LACAGEO Mini-Atlas (2013) distinguishes about 280 living languages in Cameroon. The exact number varies according to the criteria (SIL: 274, Ethnologue: 279). Value all the languages cited.

student.intro: Cameroon is one of the richest nations in the world in languages — the linguistic Mini-Atlas lists about 280! In this lesson, you discover the place of Ngiemboon in this great family.
activities: Look at the Mini-Atlas map and find the area where Ngiemboon is mainly spoken.
Copy and complete: Ngiemboon belongs to the ___ family. It is mostly spoken in the ___ region.
According to the Mini-Atlas, how many living languages are there in the Ngiemboon region? Note down this number.
Survey: ask an adult the name of the language in which they were raised and where it is spoken.
Memorise: **dialect** = an intelligible variant of the same language; **national language** = language of an ethnic group that does not extend beyond the borders of one State (ACA LAN).
student.memo: Cameroon has about **280 languages** according to the LACAGEO Mini-Atlas. Ngiemboon belongs to a Cameroonian language family and has its own dialectal variants. According to the ACA LAN, a national language is the language of an ethnic group that does not extend beyond the borders of one State.

lessons.title: Classification of languages and linguistic atlas
lessons.anelcac: Classification of the languages of Cameroon: linguistic areas, families, ALCAM atlas
objectives: Name the main linguistic areas of Cameroon
Read and interpret an extract from a linguistic atlas (ALCAM / Mini-Atlas)
Classify Ngiemboon according to its typological criteria
Producing a short text presenting Ngiemboon

teacher.intro: Lesson: Classification of languages and linguistic atlas. Module: Module I — Cameroonian linguistic diversity.
steps: **Setting the context:** Go back over the definitions. How many language families do students remember?
**Presentation:** The 8 world language families according to Ethnologue (Niger-Kordofanian, Nilo-Saharan, Afro-Asiatic…). Place Cameroonian languages within this whole.
**Explanation:** Show how to find Ngiemboon in the ALCAM: ISO code, family, location.
**Guided practice:** In pairs, students find 3 languages neighbouring Ngiemboon and note their ISO codes.
**Production:** 5-line paragraph presenting Ngiemboon (family, region, speakers, distinctive feature).
teacher.freedom: The online ALCAM is on the Mozilla Data Collective. The LACAGEO Mini-Atlas covers all the administrative regions with maps and statistics.
teacher.tips: The online ALCAM is on the Mozilla Data Collective. The LACAGEO Mini-Atlas covers all the administrative regions with maps and statistics.

student.intro: A linguistic atlas is a specialised map. The ALCAM (Atlas of the Languages of Cameroon) and the LACAGEO Mini-Atlas let you locate Ngiemboon precisely.
activities: On the Mini-Atlas map, locate Ngiemboon and note its administrative region.
List 3 languages whose area is adjacent to that of Ngiemboon.
Classify these 4 languages in a table: Language | Family | Main region.
Write an introductory paragraph about Ngiemboon with at least 5 pieces of information taken from the atlas.
Memorise: **ISO 639** = international language codes; **ALCAM** = Atlas des Langues du Cameroun.
student.memo: The **ALCAM** and the **LACAGEO Mini-Atlas** list and locate all the national languages of Cameroon. Cameroon has 8 main language families. Ngiemboon appears there with its family and its location. Knowing how to read a linguistic atlas is reading the history of peoples.

lessons.moduleTitle: Module II — Segmental phonology: vowels and consonants
lessons.title: Vowels of Ngiemboon
lessons.anelcac: AGLC vowels — simple, specific, complex
objectives: Identify the simple vowels of the phonological system of Ngiemboon
Recognising specific vowels absent from French
Pronouncing vowels correctly in the context of a word
Transcribing words containing vowels according to AGLC

teacher.intro: Lesson: Ngiemboon vowels. Module: Module II — Segmental phonology: vowels and consonants.
steps: **Setting the context:** Write known words in Ngiemboon on the board and ask which sounds students hear.
**Presentation:** Introduce the AGLC. Write the simple vowels of Ngiemboon on the board, articulating them clearly.
**Explanation:** Vowels specific to Ngiemboon that are absent from French (nasal, particular openness…). Listening and repetition exercises.
**Application:** List of 10 words — students underline the vowels and indicate: simple or specific.
**Assessment:** Dictation of 5 simple words — students transcribe them with the correct vowels.
teacher.freedom: Use the examples from the platform's ALCAM vocabulary. For each specific vowel, give a memorable key word.
teacher.tips: Use the examples from the platform's ALCAM vocabulary. For each specific vowel, give a memorable key word.

student.intro: Every language has its own sounds. In Ngiemboon, some vowels do not exist in French. This lesson teaches you to hear, pronounce and write them.
activities: Listen to the recordings of the Ngiemboon vocabulary and identify the vowels you hear.
Classify the vowels: **Shared with French** | **Specific to Ngiemboon**.
Transcribe the 5 dictated words, taking care to note each vowel correctly.
Find 3 words in Ngiemboon for each specific vowel and write them down.
Memorise: **AGLC** = Alphabet Général des Langues Camerounaises, the official reference.
student.memo: The vowel system of **Ngiemboon** includes simple vowels and specific vowels (e.g. nasalised vowels). They are written using the **AGLC**. Mastery of vowels is the basis of reading and writing in Ngiemboon.

lessons.moduleTitle: Module II — Segmental phonology: vowels and consonants
lessons.title: Ngiemboon consonants and written production
lessons.anelcac: Consonants — simple, specific, complex; written production of vowels and consonants
objectives: Identify the consonant system of Ngiemboon
Recognising specific consonants absent from French
Articulate consonants correctly in context
Writing words with vowels and consonants correctly notated

teacher.intro: Lesson: Ngiemboon consonants and written production. Module: Module II — Segmental phonology: vowels and consonants.
steps: **Setting the context:** Recall the vowels. What is a consonant?
**Presentation:** Table of Ngiemboon consonants according to the AGLC. Stress the specific consonants (labio-velars, prenasalised, implosives…).
**Explanation:** Articulating difficult consonants: in isolation → syllable → word.
**Application:** Minimal pairs: listening to words that differ only by one consonant.
**Production:** 5 simple sentences in Ngiemboon with careful consonant transcription.
teacher.freedom: Implosive and prenasalised consonants are often the most difficult for students who learned to read and write in French. Repeat the listening activities many times.
teacher.tips: Implosive and prenasalised consonants are often the most difficult for students who learned to read and write in French. Repeat the listening activities many times.

student.intro: After the vowels, here are the consonants of Ngiemboon! Some are unique — you will only hear them in Ngiemboon and in a few neighbouring African languages.
activities: Listen to the minimal pairs and tick the word you hear (e.g. bìlí / pìlí).
Transcribe 5 dictated words, paying attention to the specific consonants.
Find in the vocabulary all the words containing a prenasalised consonant. How many do you find?
Compose 3 simple sentences in Ngiemboon, each with at least one specific consonant.
Memorise: **minimal pair** = two words identical except for one phoneme.
student.memo: The consonant system of **Ngiemboon** includes consonants shared with French and specific consonants (implosives, prenasalised, labio-velars…). Writing them according to the **AGLC** is essential for reading and writing.

lessons.title: Definition and functions of tones
lessons.anelcac: Tones — definition, function, presentation; simple tones (high, low, mid)
objectives: Define tone as a distinctive feature of tone languages
Distinguish lexical tone from grammatical tone
Identify the simple tones of Ngiemboon
Transcribing words with their tones according to AGLC

teacher.intro: Lesson: Definition and function of tones. Module: Module III — Suprasegmental phonology: tones.
steps: **Setting the context:** Say two Ngiemboon words that are written the same but have different tones and different meanings.
**Presentation:** Define tone. Present the simple tones of Ngiemboon and their AGLC diacritics.
**Explanation:** Simple tones: high (´), low (`), mid (¯). Have students repeat each tone.
**Application:** Match recorded words with their tone notation.
**Assessment:** Dictation of 5 words — students note the tones.
teacher.freedom: Singing the tones helps to memorise them. Use a flute or whistle the tonal melodies.
teacher.tips: Singing the tones helps to memorise them. Use a flute or whistle the tonal melodies.

student.intro: Ngiemboon is a tonal language: the pitch of your voice changes the meaning of the word! You will learn to hear and write down these tones.
activities: Listen to the pairs of words. For each pair, are the tones the same or different?
Transcribe 5 words with their tones using the AGLC diacritics (´ ` ¯).
Find 2 words in the vocabulary that differ only in tone. What does each one mean?
Sing the tones of a 3-syllable word as High-Low-High, then Low-High-Low. What difference do you hear?
Memorise: high tone = ´ ; low tone = ` ; mid tone = ¯.
student.memo: In **Ngiemboon**, tone is phonological: it distinguishes words with different meanings. The **simple tones** are high (´), low (`), and sometimes mid (¯). They are written using the **AGLC** diacritics.

lessons.title: Complex tones and tone-marked written production
lessons.anelcac: Complex tones (rising, falling); finding the tone of a word; tonal written production
objectives: Identify the complex tones of Ngiemboon (rising, falling)
Finding the tone of a word by the isolation method
Transcribing sentences with full tone marking
Producing a short text in Ngiemboon with correct tones

teacher.intro: Lesson: Complex tones and tonal written production. Module: Module III — Suprasegmental phonology: tones.
steps: **Setting the context:** Recall the simple tones. Announce that some syllables carry two tones in succession.
**Presentation:** Complex tones: falling (̂), rising (̌). Let students hear them and reproduce them.
**Explanation:** Isolation method: say the word with an artificial high tone, then a low one, and listen to which sounds natural.
**Application:** Students find the tone of 10 words in Ngiemboon using the isolation method.
**Production:** Dialogue of 6 lines in Ngiemboon with complete tone notation.
teacher.freedom: The complex falling tone is often the most frequent. Start with it before the rising tone.
teacher.tips: The complex falling tone is often the most frequent. Start with it before the rising tone.

student.intro: You know the simple tones. Now for the complex tones of Ngiemboon — syllables that rise and fall at the same time!
activities: Listen to the recorded words and sort them: Simple tone | Complex tone.
Apply the isolation method to 5 words: say them high, then low, and note the tone you perceive.
Transcribe a dialogue of 4 lines in Ngiemboon with all the tones marked.
Write a 3-sentence text in Ngiemboon about an action from your daily life, with tone marking.
Memorise: falling tone = ̂ ; rising tone = ̌.
student.memo: The **complex tones** of **Ngiemboon** (falling ̂, rising ̌) are melodic movements on a single syllable. The **isolation method** makes it possible to find the tone of an unknown word. A transcription in Ngiemboon without tones is incomplete.

lessons.title: The noun base and noun classes
lessons.anelcac: NP: constituents, base noun + affixes, noun classes, personal pronouns
objectives: Identify the structure of the noun in Ngiemboon (base + affixes)
Recognising the noun classes of Ngiemboon
Form the singular and plural of nouns
Use the personal pronouns corresponding to noun classes

teacher.intro: Lesson: The noun base and noun classes. Module: Module IV — The noun phrase.
steps: **Setting the context:** Write a noun in Ngiemboon in the singular and plural. What changes?
**Presentation:** Noun class: in Bantu and Bantoid languages, nouns are grouped into classes marked by prefixes.
**Explanation:** Main noun classes of Ngiemboon with singular and plural prefixes.
**Application:** Table: singular → plural for 10 nouns.
**Assessment:** Identify the noun class of 5 nouns.
teacher.freedom: Start from the nouns that students already use. Noun classes often correspond to semantic categories (humans, animals, objects…).
teacher.tips: Start from the nouns that students already use. Noun classes often correspond to semantic categories (humans, animals, objects…).

student.intro: In Ngiemboon, nouns are organised into **classes**. Each class has its own prefixes for the singular and plural — a much richer system than gender in French!
activities: Using the Ngiemboon vocabulary, make a table: Singular | Plural | Noun class.
Identify the class prefix in each noun. Highlight it.
Put the following 5 nouns into the plural by changing the prefix according to the class.
Match each noun with its corresponding class pronoun.
Memorise: **noun class** = grammatical category of nouns, marked by prefixes.
student.memo: In **Ngiemboon**, nouns are organised into **noun classes** marked by prefixes. A change of prefix indicates number. Pronouns, adjectives and verbs agree with the class of the noun.

lessons.title: Noun determiners
lessons.anelcac: Determiners: possessives, demonstratives, numerals, indefinites, interrogatives; noun class agreement
objectives: Identify the different types of determiners in Ngiemboon
Make determiners agree with the noun according to the noun class
Build complex noun phrases
Producing sentences with complete NPs

teacher.intro: Lesson: Noun determiners. Module: Module IV — The noun phrase.
steps: **Setting the context:** Write a simple noun phrase. How can it be enriched?
**Presentation:** Determiners in Ngiemboon: possessives, demonstratives, numerals, indefinites, interrogatives.
**Explanation:** Each determiner agrees with the class of the noun (same class prefix or suffix).
**Application:** Complete noun phrases with the correct determiner according to the class.
**Production:** 5 complex noun phrases (noun + 2 determiners) used in sentences.
teacher.freedom: Stress class agreement — one of the most distinctive features of Ngiemboon compared with French.
teacher.tips: Stress class agreement — one of the most distinctive features of Ngiemboon compared with French.

student.intro: A noun with its determiners becomes much more precise! In Ngiemboon, determiners agree with the **noun class**.
activities: Complete the NPs with the correct possessive determiner according to the noun class.
Underline the determiners in 5 sentences in Ngiemboon and identify their type.
Turn each simple noun phrase into a complex noun phrase by adding a demonstrative and a numeral.
Write 5 sentences in Ngiemboon with at least two determiners per noun phrase.
Memorise: **class agreement** = the determiner changes form according to the noun class.
student.memo: In **Ngiemboon**, all determiners (possessives, demonstratives, numerals, indefinites, interrogatives) agree with the **noun class** of the noun. A **complex NP** = noun + nominal base + agreeing determiners.

lessons.title: The verb stem and conjugation
lessons.anelcac: VP: constituents, stem, affixes, conjugation, verb tenses
objectives: Identify the verb stem and the conjugation affixes in Ngiemboon
Conjugate a verb in the main tenses
Analyse the morphological structure of a verb form
Use verb forms correctly in sentences

teacher.intro: Lesson: The verb stem and conjugation. Module: Module V — The verb phrase.
steps: **Setting the context:** Write a verb form in Ngiemboon and ask students to identify the stem.
**Presentation:** Break down a verb form: subject prefix + TAM markers + stem + suffixes.
**Explanation:** Conjugation paradigm of a common verb in Ngiemboon in several tenses.
**Application:** Conjugation table: 3 common verbs.
**Assessment:** Translate 5 sentences from French into Ngiemboon.
teacher.freedom: The TAM system of Ngiemboon is often richer than that of French. Start with the most commonly used tenses.
teacher.tips: The TAM system of Ngiemboon is often richer than that of French. Start with the most commonly used tenses.

student.intro: The verb is the heart of the sentence in Ngiemboon. It alone carries tense, aspect, mood and subject! In this lesson, you take apart the verbal mechanics.
activities: Break down 5 verb forms in Ngiemboon: subject prefix | TAM marker | stem | suffix.
Conjugate the verb 'to eat' in Ngiemboon in 3 different tenses for all persons.
Identify the tense of 5 sentences in Ngiemboon and justify your answer.
Translate 3 sentences from French into Ngiemboon, taking care with the conjugation.
Memorise: **TAM** = Tense-Aspect-Mood; this is what verbal affixes express in Ngiemboon.
student.memo: In **Ngiemboon**, a verb form = subject prefix + TAM markers + stem + suffixes. The **TAM** (Tense-Aspect-Mood) system expresses more precise temporal and aspectual nuances than in French.

lessons.title: Verbal moods and negation
lessons.anelcac: Moods: indicative, imperative; negation; written production of simple/complex VP
objectives: Identify and use the main verbal moods of Ngiemboon
Form the verbal negation
Build simple and complex verb phrases
Producing a text with a variety of moods and aspects

teacher.intro: Lesson: Verbal moods and negation. Module: Module V — The verb phrase.
steps: **Setting the context:** Give an order in Ngiemboon. Which mood is used?
**Presentation:** Moods in Ngiemboon: indicative, imperative, and other aspectual moods.
**Explanation:** Formation of the negative in Ngiemboon: prefix, negative suffix, or particle.
**Application:** Turn 5 affirmative sentences into negative ones and vice versa.
**Production:** 8-sentence text alternating affirmation, negation and imperative.
teacher.freedom: Negation in Ngiemboon can be double (framing the verb) or simple. Show both cases.
teacher.tips: Negation in Ngiemboon can be double (framing the verb) or simple. Show both cases.

student.intro: Giving an order, expressing doubt, denying an action — each nuance has its own form in Ngiemboon!
activities: Put the 5 given sentences into the negative form.
Turn these 5 statements into imperatives addressed to a friend.
Identify the mood and polarity (affirmative/negative) of each sentence in the text provided.
Write a dialogue of 6 lines including at least 2 imperatives and 2 negations.
Memorise: **mood** = the way of viewing the action; **negation** = grammatical marker denying the action.
student.memo: In **Ngiemboon**, the main moods are the **indicative** and the **imperative**. **Negation** is marked by a particle or a specific affix. The diversity of moods is an expressive richness of Ngiemboon.

lessons.moduleTitle: Module VI — The sentence in Ngiemboon
lessons.title: The simple sentence and its types
lessons.anelcac: Simple, interrogative, negative and imperative sentence; word order
objectives: Analyse the structure of the simple sentence in Ngiemboon
Distinguish the 4 types of sentences
Mastering the order of constituents
Producing varied simple sentences

vocabulary.langText: gwɔ́ mejʉʼ mié é ge lá’a tsẅé.
vocabulary.langWord: Legÿo tà mejʉʼ mbòŋo mie é tʉ́te

teacher.intro: Lesson: The simple sentence and its types. Module: Module VI — The sentence in Ngiemboon.
steps: **Setting the context:** Read a sentence in Ngiemboon. Who does what?
**Presentation:** Basic constituent order in Ngiemboon. Compare with French.
**Explanation:** The 4 sentence types from the same basic sentence.
**Application:** Turn declarative sentences into interrogative ones, then into negative ones.
**Production:** 8 varied sentences (2 per type) about school life.
teacher.freedom: Word order in Ngiemboon may differ from French. This is a typological feature, not a mistake.
teacher.tips: Word order in Ngiemboon may differ from French. This is a typological feature, not a mistake.

student.intro: A well-constructed sentence in Ngiemboon follows precise rules. You learn the types of sentences and word order.
activities: Identify the order of constituents in 5 sentences in Ngiemboon.
Turn 4 declarative sentences into yes/no questions.
Turn these 4 sentences into negatives.
Write 2 sentences of each type (declarative, interrogative, negative, imperative).
Memorise: the basic order in **Ngiemboon** is typologically stable.
student.memo: The **simple sentence** in **Ngiemboon** has a characteristic order of constituents. The 4 types (declarative, interrogative, negative, imperative) are formed with specific grammatical markers.

lessons.moduleTitle: Module VI — The sentence in Ngiemboon
lessons.title: Logical connectors and the complex sentence
lessons.anelcac: Logical connectors, complex sentence, coordination, subordination; written production
objectives: Identify the logical connectors of Ngiemboon
Distinguish coordination from subordination
Build complex sentences
Producing a coherent text with syntactic variety

vocabulary.langText: gwɔ́ mejʉʼ mié é ge lá’a tsẅé.
vocabulary.langWord: Legÿo tà mejʉʼ mbòŋo mie é tʉ́te

teacher.intro: Lesson: Logical connectors and the complex sentence. Module: Module VI — The sentence in Ngiemboon.
steps: **Setting the context:** Read a short story in Ngiemboon. Which words link the sentences?
**Presentation:** Connectors in Ngiemboon: coordinating and subordinating conjunctions.
**Explanation:** Complex sentence by coordination / by subordination. Examples in Ngiemboon.
**Application:** Link 5 pairs of simple sentences with the appropriate connector.
**Production:** 10-sentence text on 'A day in my village' with 5 different connectors.
teacher.freedom: The connectors of Ngiemboon often have French equivalents but with different syntactic positions.
teacher.tips: The connectors of Ngiemboon often have French equivalents but with different syntactic positions.

student.intro: To tell stories and argue, you need to link your sentences. The **logical connectors** of Ngiemboon are your tools!
activities: Underline all the connectors in the text provided.
Classify them: Addition | Cause | Consequence | Opposition | Time.
Link 5 pairs of sentences with the most appropriate connector.
Write a text of 8 sentences with at least 4 different connectors.
Memorise: coordination = same level; subordination = one sentence inside another.
student.memo: In **Ngiemboon**, **logical connectors** make it possible to build coherent **complex sentences**. Varying syntactic structures improves the quality of written and spoken expression.

lessons.title: Greeting, introducing yourself and interacting in Ngiemboon
lessons.anelcac: Everyday communication situations: greetings, introductions, polite expressions
objectives: Mastering greeting formulas according to context
Introducing yourself and someone else in Ngiemboon
Use polite and respectful expressions
Holding a short everyday conversation

teacher.intro: Lesson: Greeting, introducing yourself and interacting in Ngiemboon. Module: Module VII — Everyday life (Level 1).
steps: **Setting the context:** Two students meet at the market. Act out the scene in French, then ask how to say it in Ngiemboon.
**Presentation:** Greetings in Ngiemboon according to the time of day, age and context.
**Explanation:** Formulas of respect towards elders, specific to Ngiemboon culture.
**Role play:** In groups of 2, simulate encounters in various contexts (market, school, ceremony).
**Production:** Dialogue of 10 lines between two people of different generations.
teacher.freedom: Greeting rules reflect deep cultural values. Value the knowledge of students from families who speak the language.
teacher.tips: Greeting rules reflect deep cultural values. Value the knowledge of students from families who speak the language.

student.intro: Knowing how to greet in Ngiemboon means respecting the culture! The greetings change depending on whom you greet and at what time.
activities: Complete the table of Ngiemboon greetings: Time | Formula | Expected response.
Play role A: greeting an elder at the morning market.
Make up a dialogue of 8 lines between a child and their grandfather.
Note down 3 Ngiemboon politeness formulas with no direct equivalent in French.
Memorise the morning and evening greeting formulas, and those for elders, in Ngiemboon.
student.memo: **Greetings** in **Ngiemboon** vary according to the time of day, status and social context. They reflect the community's values of respect and solidarity.

lessons.title: Express everyday needs and actions
lessons.anelcac: Real-life situations: shopping, requests for help, travelling, daily activities
objectives: Express everyday needs in Ngiemboon
Describe daily activities
Use vocabulary for places and actions of everyday life
Producing a descriptive text on a typical day

teacher.intro: Lesson: Expressing everyday needs and actions. Module: Module VII — Everyday life (Level 1).
steps: **Setting the context:** Images of scenes from daily life — market, field, school, home. How can they be described in Ngiemboon?
**Presentation:** Thematic vocabulary: food, travel, household activities.
**Simulation:** Market scene: buyer and seller in Ngiemboon.
**Application:** Describe your day in Ngiemboon (from waking up to going to bed).
**Production:** 10-sentence text: 'My day in Ngiemboon'.
teacher.freedom: Everyday vocabulary is the most motivating. Link the ALCAM words to real situations.
teacher.tips: Everyday vocabulary is the most motivating. Link the ALCAM words to real situations.

student.intro: You know how to greet people. Now you are going to manage in everyday situations in Ngiemboon: at the market, on the road, at home.
activities: Match each picture of a scene from daily life with the corresponding word or sentence in Ngiemboon.
Play the role of the seller at the market: answer the requests in Ngiemboon.
Write 5 sentences describing your morning activities from the time you wake up.
Translate these 5 sentences about daily journeys into Ngiemboon.
Memorise 10 everyday words in Ngiemboon with their French translation.
student.memo: The **everyday** vocabulary in **Ngiemboon** covers food, getting around and household activities. Mastering it allows functional communication in all contexts.

lessons.title: Argue and persuade in Ngiemboon
lessons.anelcac: Elaborate communication: argumentation, narration, formal speech
objectives: Build a simple argument in Ngiemboon
Use the expressions of formal speech
Narrating a past event coherently
Delivering a 2-minute oral speech in Ngiemboon

teacher.intro: Lesson: Arguing and persuading in Ngiemboon. Module: Module VIII — Everyday life (Level 2).
steps: **Setting the context:** Read a proverb in Ngiemboon. Ask students to explain it and defend it.
**Presentation:** Formulas of formal oral speech in Ngiemboon: forms of address, opening, closing.
**Explanation:** Structure of an argument: thesis → arguments → examples → conclusion.
**Practice:** Debate: for or against the use of Ngiemboon at school? Each group defends its position.
**Production:** 2-minute speech on a given theme.
teacher.freedom: Public speaking is highly valued in Cameroonian cultures. Draw on this tradition to motivate the students.
teacher.tips: Public speaking is highly valued in Cameroonian cultures. Draw on this tradition to motivate the students.

student.intro: In Ngiemboon cultures, well-spoken words are a force. You learn to argue and persuade with eloquence.
activities: Identify in the text: thesis, arguments, examples.
Prepare 3 arguments to defend the teaching of Ngiemboon in primary school.
Give an opening speech for a ceremony in Ngiemboon.
Narration: tell in Ngiemboon about a memorable event from your school life.
Memorise the opening and closing formulas of a formal speech in Ngiemboon.
student.memo: **Argumentation** in **Ngiemboon** follows this pattern: thesis → arguments → examples → conclusion. **Formal speech** follows precise cultural conventions. Mastery of elaborate oral expression is a high-level skill.

lessons.title: Oral literature and advanced written production
lessons.anelcac: Oral literature: proverbs, tales, riddles; long written production
objectives: Analyse the structure of a tale or a riddle in Ngiemboon
Identify the themes and values conveyed
Writing a short tale following the conventions of the genre
Using oral literature as a teaching resource

teacher.intro: Lesson: Oral literature and advanced written production. Module: Module VIII — Everyday life (Level 2).
steps: **Setting the context:** Tell or play a short tale in Ngiemboon.
**Presentation:** Genres of oral literature: tales, proverbs, riddles, epics.
**Analysis:** Structure of the tale: initial situation → disruption → events → resolution → moral.
**Application:** Analyse a tale provided, following this structure.
**Production:** Tale of at least 15 lines in Ngiemboon with an explicit moral.
teacher.freedom: Oral literature is a threatened cultural treasure. Invite community storytellers if possible.
teacher.tips: Oral literature is a threatened cultural treasure. Invite community storytellers if possible.

student.intro: Ngiemboon tales, proverbs and riddles are literary works in their own right. You will analyse them and you will create your own!
activities: Read the tale provided and identify the 5 stages of its narrative structure.
Identify 3 moral values taught by this tale.
Translate a proverb in Ngiemboon into French and explain its figurative meaning.
Write a short tale (15 lines) in Ngiemboon with a moral about work or respect.
Memorise: tale = fictional narrative with an educational purpose; proverb = brief formula of collective wisdom.
student.memo: The **oral literature** of **Ngiemboon** (tales, proverbs, riddles) transmits the values of the community. The tale has a 5-stage structure. Writing it in Ngiemboon draws on all the language skills acquired.

lessons.title: Cultural areas of Cameroon
lessons.anelcac: Cultural areas: Beti-Fang, Grassfield, Sawa, Sudano-Sahelian
objectives: Identify the four major cultural areas of Cameroon
Locating Ngiemboon culture within its cultural area
Describe the distinctive features of each area
Valuing cultural diversity as a national asset

teacher.intro: Lesson: Cultural areas of Cameroon. Module: Module MC1 — Cameroonian cultural diversity.
steps: **Setting the context:** Display the map of the cultural Mini-Atlas. Ask students to locate their culture.
**Presentation:** The 4 areas: Beti-Fang (Centre-South), Grassfields (West-North-West), Sawa (coast), Sudano-Sahelian (north).
**Explanation:** Cultural characteristics of each area: social organisation, agriculture, art, music.
**Application:** Each student presents 3 cultural elements from their area.
**Assessment:** Map to complete + short comparative text.
teacher.freedom: Value every culture. Avoid cultural hierarchies. Diversity is a richness.
teacher.tips: Value every culture. Avoid cultural hierarchies. Diversity is a richness.

student.intro: Cameroon is 'Africa in miniature' — its cultural diversity is extraordinary. Ngiemboon culture belongs to a specific area that you are going to discover.
activities: On the Mini-Atlas map, colour the 4 cultural areas in different colours.
Note down which area the Ngiemboon community is located in.
List 3 distinctive cultural traits of this area (food, housing, social organisation).
Compare two areas: what do they have in common? What sets them apart?
Memorise the 4 major cultural areas and their locations.
student.memo: Cameroon has 4 major **cultural areas**: **Beti-Fang**, **Grassfields**, **Sawa** and **Sudano-Sahelian**. The Ngiemboon community belongs to one of them, with its specific practices and values.

lessons.title: Ngiemboon culture in the Cameroonian context
lessons.anelcac: Cultural identity, intangible heritage, languages and cultures
objectives: Define the notion of cultural identity
Describe the constituent elements of Ngiemboon culture
Linking language and culture
Producing a presentation on Ngiemboon culture

teacher.intro: Lesson: Ngiemboon culture in the Cameroonian context. Module: Module MC1 — Cameroonian cultural diversity.
steps: **Setting the context:** What makes you different from students of another region?
**Presentation:** Elements of Ngiemboon culture: language, music, gastronomy, values, social organisation.
**Explanation:** Intangible heritage: what cannot be seen but is passed on.
**Research:** Students survey their families about a Ngiemboon cultural element.
**Production:** 3-minute oral presentation on an element of Ngiemboon heritage.
teacher.freedom: Turning the class into a living museum: each student brings an object, a recipe, a proverb.
teacher.tips: Turning the class into a living museum: each student brings an object, a recipe, a proverb.

student.intro: Your language is also your culture. You are going to explore what makes Ngiemboon culture rich.
activities: List 5 elements of Ngiemboon culture: language, music, cooking, values, organisation.
Choose an element of Ngiemboon intangible heritage and describe it in 5 sentences.
Prepare a 3-minute oral presentation (outline: introduction → description → importance).
With your classmates, create a poster of Ngiemboon culture.
Memorise: **intangible heritage** = cultural knowledge and practices transmitted orally.
student.memo: Ngiemboon **cultural identity** is expressed through language, music, gastronomy and social organisation. **Intangible heritage** is as precious as material monuments.

lessons.title: Culinary and musical practices of the Ngiemboon community
lessons.anelcac: Ways of life: culinary practices, musical practices
objectives: Describe the traditional culinary practices of Ngiemboon
Identify musical instruments and genres
Explain the social role of music and cooking
Presenting a recipe or a musical genre in Ngiemboon

teacher.intro: Lesson: Culinary and musical practices of the Ngiemboon community. Module: Module MC2 — Ways of life.
steps: **Setting the context:** Bring a traditional food associated with Ngiemboon. Prompt a discussion.
**Presentation:** Dishes, ingredients and cooking techniques. Instruments and musical genres.
**Demonstration:** Play a traditional piece of music from the region. Identify the instruments.
**Application:** Describe in Ngiemboon the preparation of a simple dish.
**Production:** Oral presentation: a recipe or a musical genre.
teacher.freedom: Food and music are emotional gateways into a culture. Use as many concrete examples as possible.
teacher.tips: Food and music are emotional gateways into a culture. Use as many concrete examples as possible.

student.intro: The cooking and music of Ngiemboon culture tell who you are. You explore them as living cultural expressions.
activities: Describe in Ngiemboon the steps for preparing a traditional dish.
Identify 3 traditional musical instruments and explain how they are used.
Transcribe the text of a simple traditional song in Ngiemboon and translate it.
Present a recipe in Ngiemboon orally (minimum 6 steps).
Memorise the names of the main dishes and instruments in Ngiemboon.
student.memo: Traditional **cooking** and **music** are strong markers of identity in Ngiemboon culture. Dishes, instruments and musical genres often have names in Ngiemboon that do not translate exactly.

lessons.title: Traditional housing and clothing of the Ngiemboon community
lessons.anelcac: Ways of life: clothing and architectural practices
objectives: Describe the traditional dwelling of the Ngiemboon community
Identify clothing and its meaning
Explain how ways of life have changed
Producing a descriptive text on housing or clothing

teacher.intro: Lesson: Traditional housing and clothing of the Ngiemboon community. Module: Module MC2 — Ways of life.
steps: **Setting the context:** Photos of traditional and modern dwellings. What has changed?
**Presentation:** Types of dwellings: materials, shape, organisation of space.
**Explanation:** Clothing: colours, fabrics, accessories and social meanings.
**Analysis:** Which traditional elements persist? Which have changed?
**Production:** Illustrated descriptive text on a dwelling or an outfit.
teacher.freedom: Avoid exoticising presentations. Understand the cultural logic behind forms of housing and clothing.
teacher.tips: Avoid exoticising presentations. Understand the cultural logic behind forms of housing and clothing.

student.intro: The house and traditional clothing tell about the social organisation and values of Ngiemboon culture.
activities: Describe in Ngiemboon the materials and layout of a traditional dwelling.
Explain the meaning of an outfit worn at a ceremony.
Compare traditional and modern housing: 3 differences, 2 common points.
Write a text of 10 sentences on the evolution of housing in the Ngiemboon community.
Memorise the Ngiemboon vocabulary of housing and clothing.
student.memo: The **traditional housing** and **clothing** of Ngiemboon culture reflect specific values: family organisation, social roles, relationship to the sacred.

lessons.title: Birth and initiation rites in Ngiemboon culture
lessons.anelcac: Key events: birth, raising children, initiation rites
objectives: Describe the practices linked to birth in Ngiemboon culture
Explain the role of initiation rites
Analyse the traditional education of the child
Producing a text on education in the Ngiemboon tradition

teacher.intro: Lesson: Birth and initiation rites in Ngiemboon culture. Module: Module MC3 — Key life events.
steps: **Setting the context:** What do students know about the practices surrounding birth in their family?
**Presentation:** Birth rites: naming, presentation to the family, ceremonies.
**Explanation:** Traditional education: the role of elders, learning by imitation.
**Discussion:** Initiation rites: their meaning, content, contemporary evolution.
**Production:** Narrative text on a birth or initiation rite.
teacher.freedom: Some rites are confidential. Do not force students to share. Work on the public aspects.
teacher.tips: Some rites are confidential. Do not force students to share. Work on the public aspects.

student.intro: In Ngiemboon culture, being born and growing up are social events — the whole community takes part in the child's upbringing.
activities: In 5 sentences, describe a rite surrounding birth in Ngiemboon culture.
Explain the role of grandparents in traditional education.
Compare traditional and school education: 3 complementarities, 2 tensions.
Write an imaginary letter from a grandfather to his grandchild passing on a value.
Memorise the names of the main stages of life in Ngiemboon.
student.memo: In **Ngiemboon** culture, **birth** and **initiation** are moments of intense socialisation. Traditional education rests on oral transmission and the role of elders.

lessons.title: Marriage, mourning and celebrations in Ngiemboon culture
lessons.anelcac: Key events: marriage, death and mourning, ceremonies
objectives: Describe the marriage practices of Ngiemboon
Analyse funeral rites
Explain the social importance of ceremonies
Producing an account of a ceremony

teacher.intro: Lesson: Marriage, mourning and celebrations in Ngiemboon culture. Module: Module MC3 — Key life events.
steps: **Setting the context:** Photos of ceremonies (wedding, funeral). What do students observe?
**Presentation:** Traditional marriage: bride price, ceremonies, role of the families.
**Explanation:** Funerals and mourning: duration, stages, social obligations.
**Analysis:** Why do these ceremonies strengthen community ties?
**Production:** Account of an imaginary ceremony (10-15 sentences).
teacher.freedom: Approach mourning with sensitivity. Some students may have recently experienced a bereavement.
teacher.tips: Approach mourning with sensitivity. Some students may have recently experienced a bereavement.

student.intro: Marriage and funerals in Ngiemboon culture are social acts that bind the community together.
activities: Describe the stages of traditional marriage in chronological order.
Explain the symbolic meaning of the bride price in Ngiemboon culture.
Describe how mourning is handled in Ngiemboon culture.
Write a text of 12 sentences telling the story of a marriage ceremony.
Memorise the vocabulary of marriage and mourning in Ngiemboon.
student.memo: **Marriage** and **mourning** in **Ngiemboon** culture are structuring community events. The bride price, ceremonies and funeral rites express the values of solidarity and respect for the ancestors.

lessons.title: Traditional games and social organisation in Ngiemboon culture
lessons.anelcac: Community practices Level 1: games, traditional economy, social organisation
objectives: Describe traditional games and their educational role
Explain the social organisation of the Ngiemboon community
Identify traditional institutions (chiefdom, council of elders)
Producing a text on social organisation

teacher.intro: Lesson: Traditional games and social organisation in Ngiemboon culture. Module: Module MC4 — Community practices (Level 1).
steps: **Setting the context:** Name a traditional game of the community and explain its rules.
**Presentation:** Traditional games of Ngiemboon: rules, materials, ages and genders involved.
**Explanation:** Social organisation: chiefdom, council of elders, societies, age groups.
**Application:** Diagram of the community's social organisation.
**Production:** Text on the role of the chief or the council of elders.
teacher.freedom: Traditional games are often metaphors for social organisation. Make use of this link.
teacher.tips: Traditional games are often metaphors for social organisation. Make use of this link.

student.intro: Games transmit values. And the social organisation of Ngiemboon is a sophisticated collective work.
activities: Describe the rules of a traditional game in Ngiemboon (at least 6 rules).
Explain what this game teaches children.
Draw or describe the diagram of the community's social organisation.
Write 8 sentences on the role of the council of elders in resolving conflicts.
Memorise the names of the main social institutions in Ngiemboon.
student.memo: **Ngiemboon** culture has a structured **social organisation**: chiefdom, council of elders, age groups. **Traditional games** transmit the values and skills needed for community life.

lessons.title: Traditional economy of the Ngiemboon community
lessons.anelcac: Traditional economy: farming, livestock, crafts, trade, solidarity
objectives: Describe the traditional economic activities of Ngiemboon
Explain systems of exchange and solidarity
Analyse the evolution of the traditional economy
Producing a text on an economic activity

teacher.intro: Lesson: Traditional economy of the Ngiemboon community. Module: Module MC4 — Community practices (Level 1).
steps: **Setting the context:** What did the Ngiemboon community live on before colonisation?
**Presentation:** Agriculture, livestock farming, hunting, fishing, crafts: activities and technical knowledge.
**Explanation:** Economic solidarity: tontines, agricultural mutual aid, periodic markets.
**Analysis:** The impact of monetisation and modernity.
**Production:** Descriptive text on a traditional economic activity.
teacher.freedom: The traditional economy is often invisible in textbooks. Making it visible means valuing real and complex knowledge.
teacher.tips: The traditional economy is often invisible in textbooks. Making it visible means valuing real and complex knowledge.

student.intro: The traditional economy of Ngiemboon is a sophisticated system of solidarity and know-how.
activities: List the 5 main economic activities and the knowledge they require.
Explain how a tontine or an agricultural mutual-aid system works.
Compare a traditional market and a modern market: 3 differences.
Write 10 sentences about a traditional craft activity.
Memorise the traditional economic vocabulary in Ngiemboon.
student.memo: The **traditional economy** of Ngiemboon rests on farming, crafts and solidarity systems such as tontines. These practices have a complex internal logic that coexists with the modern economy.

lessons.title: Symbolism, rites and taboos in Ngiemboon culture
lessons.anelcac: Community practices Level 2: symbolism, rites, taboos
objectives: Explain the role of symbols in Ngiemboon culture
Identify specific rites and their meaning
Analyse the social function of taboos
Producing an analytical text on a symbolic practice

teacher.intro: Lesson: Symbolism, rites and taboos in Ngiemboon culture. Module: Module MC5 — Community practices (Level 2).
steps: **Setting the context:** Show a symbolic object or colour of Ngiemboon. What does it mean?
**Presentation:** Cultural symbols: colours, objects, gestures, sacred spaces.
**Explanation:** Specific rites and their logic. Taboos: forbidden foods, places, actions.
**Discussion:** The function of taboos: protection, social cohesion, transmission of values.
**Production:** Analysis of a rite or taboo (description → meaning → social function).
teacher.freedom: Approach rites and taboos with respect and neutrality. The aim is to understand, not to judge.
teacher.tips: Approach rites and taboos with respect and neutrality. The aim is to understand, not to judge.

student.intro: Every gesture, every colour, every taboo in Ngiemboon culture has a meaning. You decode the cultural symbolism of your community.
activities: Identify 3 important symbols of Ngiemboon culture and explain their meaning.
Describe a cultural rite and analyse its social function.
Explain why cultural taboos are social regulators.
Write an analytical text of 10 sentences on a food or spatial taboo.
Memorise the Ngiemboon vocabulary of rites, symbols and taboos.
student.memo: The **symbolism** of **Ngiemboon** culture expresses a coherent system of values. **Rites** and **taboos** have a function of social regulation and of passing values on to following generations.

lessons.title: Traditional media and cultural transmission in Ngiemboon
lessons.anelcac: Community practices Level 2: traditional media, intergenerational transmission
objectives: Identify traditional media of communication in Ngiemboon culture
Analyse the mechanisms of intergenerational cultural transmission
Assess the contemporary challenges of transmission
Producing a cultural promotion project

teacher.intro: Lesson: Traditional media and cultural transmission in Ngiemboon. Module: Module MC5 — Community practices (Level 2).
steps: **Setting the context:** Before radio and the internet, how did news circulate in the Ngiemboon community?
**Presentation:** Traditional media: talking drum, town criers, griots, village meetings, evening tales.
**Explanation:** Transmission mechanisms: word of mouth, learning by example, initiation ceremonies.
**Analysis:** Contemporary challenges: rural exodus, digital media, young people's lack of interest.
**Production:** Class project to promote Ngiemboon culture (school radio, bilingual newspaper, exhibition).
teacher.freedom: Ending with a concrete project to promote culture strengthens engagement and gives meaning to the whole of the CN learning.
teacher.tips: Ending with a concrete project to promote culture strengthens engagement and gives meaning to the whole of the CN learning.

student.intro: How does a culture survive? Through its **traditional media** and its **intergenerational transmission**. In this final lesson, you think about how to protect Ngiemboon culture today.
activities: Identify 4 traditional media and explain the role of each.
Interview an elder about a piece of Ngiemboon cultural knowledge they learned from their parents. Write up their account.
Identify 3 challenges to the transmission of Ngiemboon culture and suggest solutions.
Design an enhancement project: what format, what audience, what content?
Memorise the names of the main traditional media in Ngiemboon.
student.memo: The **traditional media** of **Ngiemboon** culture (tam-tam, storytellers, village meetings) ensure the transmission of knowledge and values. Concrete actions to promote them are needed to ensure the survival of this heritage.
